constraint_decided_it: S1 Matter Removal's scope note names this exact case ('taking a tissue sample from a body') and prescribes 'multiple instantiation with adequate concepts of creating the respective items'; its subclass S2 Sample Taking carries O3 sampled from (S2 -> S10, and S10 is declared superclass of E18, so the E20 moth qualifies) and O5 removed (S2 -> S13). A applies that branch with every domain/range holding; B never reaches it and instead leans on t1536, where Doerr's 'violates identity criteria of classes' rejects the *diminished source* being reclassified as human-made, not the identity-transfer proposition B attributes to it.
better_modelling: Two chained events in the CRMsci branch, which neither answer gives in full: (1) the clipping is an S2 Sample Taking, O3 sampled from -> the pinned moth (E20, unchanged identity, merely P112 diminished if the E80 multiple instantiation is also asserted, since S1 is superclass of both S2 and E80), O5 removed -> the leg as an S13 Sample; (2) the DNA extraction is a second event over the leg -- an E81 Transformation (P124 transformed -> the leg, P123 resulted in -> the extract) or a CRMsci sub-sampling step -- yielding the frozen extract as a further S13 Sample under its own catalogue number. S13 (subclass of S11 Amount of Matter, which explicitly waives the stability-of-form that E18 requires) is the right home for a dissolved extract. Paratype status attaches to the moth only; the extract inherits provenance through the event chain, never identity.
reasoning: A's constructs all check out against their declarations (O3 S2->S10 with S10 superclass of E18; O5 S2->S13; S1 superclass of S2 and E80) and its three issue332 quotes and both scope-note quotes verify verbatim, but it collapses the clipping and the dissolution into one S2 event, so O5 points at the extract when the thing actually removed by that activity is the leg -- a missing event, hence suboptimal. B's core chain (P112/P113 E80->E18, P124/P123 E81->E18, P108 E12->E24 with the extract as E22+E20, matching CRM's own '(E22,E20)' mummy example) is domain/range-clean and correctly two-stepped, but it is the general vocabulary where the CRM offers a more specific one, and its load-bearing archive claim is misattributed: t1536 message [10] rejects the diminished natural object becoming human-made, not 'letting a removed part carry the original's identity', and Sanderson never argues that proposition at all. B also invokes 'Modelling principles > Disjointness' for a question of individual identity, which that section (class-level disjointness) does not address.
